status: frozen after the gas-only CPR0-0.6 result and before constructing or scoring local BCG stellar densities
question: Does adding the observed, deprojected BCG stellar density rescue one shared local-density response across BCG dynamics and CLASH lensing?
added_dataset: Tian et al. 2020 CDS table1.dat: total BCG stellar mass, HST effective radius, and central evaluation radius for all 20 CLASH clusters

observable_construction.stellar_profile: Hernquist rho_star=M_star*a/[2*pi*r*(r+a)^3] with a=0.551*Re, exactly matching the deprojection convention in Tian et al. 2020
observable_construction.central_points: all 20 CLASH rows below 100 kpc use the measured BCG stellar density; ACCEPT gas is added only when the radius lies inside measured profile coverage
observable_construction.outer_points: the 52 no-extrapolation ACCEPT points at 100-600 kpc from CPR0-0.6, plus the much smaller Hernquist BCG density
observable_construction.missing_central_gas: set to zero only where ACCEPT has no measured shell; Tian et al. state hot gas is subdominant to BCG stars inside Re
observable_construction.satellite_and_ICL_local_density: not available and not added; the gas-density scale bracket covers a larger fractional correction at outer radii

cross_validation.objective: equal-domain mean of equal-system mean squared log10 acceleration residual

claim_boundary: This is an added-data sensitivity motivated by the already inspected gas-only result, not pristine external validation.
The stellar density is directly tied to observed mass and size but retains the Hernquist and constant mass-to-light assumptions of Tian et al.
Satellite-galaxy and intracluster-light local densities remain unmeasured; they are most relevant outside the BCG.
The CLASH acceleration target still lacks public radial covariance and still assumes a spherical NFW deprojection.
No relativistic photon-propagation law has yet been derived for CPR0.
